chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Backbiting is more rapid in consuming the religion of the Muslim man than food is in his belly.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Sitting in the mosque awaiting the prayer is worship as long as nothing occurs.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what occurs?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Backbiting.'
ai.seo_question: How does backbiting affect a Muslim's religion according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to emphasize that backbiting is a spiritual corrosive that consumes faith more rapidly than physical food, a metaphor highlighting its invisible yet destructive nature. The hadith further contextualizes the virtue of sitting in the mosque for prayer (intizar al-salah) by noting that it is invalidated if accompanied by backbiting, illustrating how a single major sin can nullify the reward of a righteous act.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The backbiting is more quickly (absorbing) in the Religion of the Muslim man than the meal is in his inside’.
Heasws said: ‘And Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The sitting in the Masjid awaiting the Salāt is (an act of) worship for as long as ‘it’ does not occur’.
It was said, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!  And what is occurrence?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The backbiting’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Backbiting destroys the religion of a person faster than an internal cancerous disease.’ “

The Imam has also said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “Sitting in the mosque is worship as long as it does not happen.” He was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, ‘What has not happened?’ He said, ‘Backbiting.’”
